newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal's prime minister Chand sworn in.
newsitem.headline: Nepal's prime minister Chand sworn in.

text.p: Lokendra Bahadur Chand was sworn in as Nepal's new prime minister on Wednesday by King Birendra after naming a hardline communist as his deputy.
Chand named seven cabinet members, a royal palace communique said.
"His Majesty the King has...appointed the council of ministers and allocated portfolios," the communique said.
Along with the portfolio of prime minister, Chand will take charge of defence and royal palace affairs.

Bam Dev Gautam, a hardliner from the Communist Unified Marxist-Leninist (UML) party which provides crucial support to Chand, was named the deputy prime minister and given the crucial home (interior) ministry in addition to 10 other portfolios.
The new cabinet has four ministers from the UML, one from Chand's Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP) and two from the Nepal Sadbhavana Party (NSP), the minor partner in the coalition.
Sahana Pradhan, the only woman member in the new government, also belongs to the UML. She will look after the forest and soil conservation portfolios.

The RPP's Rabindra Nath Sharma, a key aide who was instrumental in securing Chand's third stint as the Himalayan kingdom's prime minister, was given charge of the finance and foreign ministries, as well as five others.
Party officials said the cabinet list was approved after intensive bargaining within the constituents of the coalition which delayed Chand's oath-taking ceremony by over 24 hours.
Chand is required to prove his majority in parliament within a month.
Party officials said the cabinet would be expanded after the parliamentary confidence vote, and portfolios held by the UML's Gautam were likely to go to his party colleagues.

Chand's RPP joined hands with the communists and the NSP last week to topple Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba, who had headed a three-party coalition led by his centrist Nepali Congress and including the RPP for 17 months.

Deuba's government was undermined by charges of corruption and the RPP's allegations that Nepali Congress dominated the coalition. Deuba resigned last Thursday but stayed on as caretaker prime minister.
